```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
```

> **In this step** we test whether the results from Step 2 can be trusted. We
> run four checks:
>
> 1. **Completeness:** was every probe fitted, and are all fractions valid?
> 2. **Independent refit:** does a different optimiser give the same answer?
> 3. **Residual diagnostics:** do the model's assumptions look reasonable?
> 4. **Sensitivity analyses:** do the conclusions change if we make different,
>    defensible modelling choices?
>
> **Reads:** `data/processed/immvar.rds` (Step 1) and `results/models/*.rds` (Step 2)<br>
> **Writes:** check tables in `results/tables/`, diagnostic figures in
> `results/figures/`, and `results/checks.txt`<br>
> **Run time:** about 2 minutes the first time; seconds when saved
> sensitivity fits exist

# Setup and data

```{r packages}
.libPaths(c("library", .libPaths()))
library(variancePartition)
library(BiocParallel)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
```

We load the same analysis cohort and formulas used in Step 2.

```{r load}
data <- readRDS("data/processed/immvar.rds")
expression <- data$expression[, data$metadata$included]
metadata   <- droplevels(data$metadata[data$metadata$included, ])
metadata$Age <- as.numeric(scale(metadata$Age))

models <- list(
  Combined = readRDS("results/models/combined.rds"),
  CD4_T    = readRDS("results/models/CD4_T.rds"),
  Monocyte = readRDS("results/models/Monocyte.rds")
)

# The same formulas as Step 2
combined_formula <- ~ Age + (1 | Sex) + (1 | CellType) + (1 | Batch) + (1 | Individual)
within_formula   <- ~ Age + (1 | Sex) + (1 | Batch) + (1 | Individual)
```

# Check 1: every probe fitted, every fraction valid

A model can fail to converge for some probes, and variancePartition would then
silently drop them. Here we confirm that each model returned **every** probe,
and that every fraction is finite, nonnegative and adds up to 1.

```{r check-completeness}
fit_counts <- data.frame()
for (name in names(models)) {
  result <- models[[name]]
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(result), rownames(expression)),
            all(is.finite(as.matrix(result))),
            all(as.matrix(result) >= 0),
            max(abs(rowSums(result) - 1)) < 1e-6)
  fit_counts <- rbind(fit_counts, data.frame(
    model     = name,
    attempted = nrow(expression),
    fitted    = nrow(result),
    failed    = nrow(expression) - nrow(result)
  ))
}
fwrite(fit_counts, "results/tables/model_fit_counts.csv")
fit_counts
```

# Check 2: an independent refit

Fitting a mixed model means numerically searching for the variance values that
best explain the data. The algorithm that does the search is called an
**optimiser**. If a different optimiser lands on the same answer, we can be
confident the original result is not an artefact of the search getting stuck.

We refit **53 probes** in each model: our three examples plus 50 chosen at
random. We call `lme4::lmer()` directly with the `bobyqa` optimiser and then
compare the fractions.

```{r independent-refit}
set.seed(20261104)
example_ids <- c("8177232", "8157524", "7903765")  # KDM5D, TLR4, GSTM1
audit_ids   <- unique(c(example_ids, sample(rownames(expression), 50)))

control <- lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", calc.derivs = FALSE,
                             optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000))

audit         <- list()
residual_data <- list()  # kept for Check 3

for (name in names(models)) {
  samples     <- if (name == "Combined") rep(TRUE, nrow(metadata)) else metadata$CellType == name
  sample_data <- droplevels(metadata[samples, ])
  formula     <- if (name == "Combined") combined_formula else within_formula

  for (id in audit_ids) {
    sample_data$expression <- as.numeric(expression[id, samples])

    # A variance estimated at zero gives a harmless "singular fit" message.
    fit <- suppressMessages(lme4::lmer(update(formula, expression ~ .), sample_data,
                                       REML = FALSE, control = control))

    independent <- calcVarPart(fit)
    original    <- as.numeric(models[[name]][id, names(independent)])

    audit[[paste(name, id)]] <- data.frame(
      model                = name,
      probe_id             = id,
      component            = names(independent),
      pipeline_fraction    = original,
      independent_fraction = unname(independent),
      absolute_difference  = abs(original - unname(independent))
    )

    if (name == "Combined" && id %in% example_ids) {
      residual_data[[id]] <- data.frame(
        probe_id              = id,
        fitted                = fitted(fit),
        standardized_residual = residuals(fit) / sigma(fit)
      )
    }
  }
}

audit <- rbindlist(audit)
fwrite(audit, "results/tables/independent_fit_check.csv")
stopifnot(max(audit$absolute_difference) < 0.01)  # stop if any fraction differs by > 1 point

audit[, .(probes = uniqueN(probe_id),
          largest_difference_in_percentage_points = 100 * max(absolute_difference)),
      by = model]
```

**Result:** the two optimisers agree to within
**`r signif(100 * max(audit$absolute_difference), 2)` percentage points** for
every component of every probe checked.

# Check 3: residual diagnostics

A linear mixed model assumes that, once all the terms are accounted for, the
leftover variation (the **residuals**) is roughly normal and has a similar
spread everywhere. We check this for the three example probes with two
standard plots:

* **Residuals vs fitted (top):** we want a shapeless cloud centred on zero.
  Separate clusters are fine. They simply reflect groups with different
  average expression, such as the two cell types.
* **Normal Q–Q (bottom):** if the residuals are normal, the points follow the
  straight line. Departures in the tails indicate outlying arrays.

```{r residual-plots, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
residual_data <- rbindlist(residual_data)
residual_data$gene <- c("8177232" = "KDM5D", "8157524" = "TLR4",
                        "7903765" = "GSTM1")[residual_data$probe_id]

residual_plot <- ggplot(residual_data, aes(fitted, standardized_residual)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~ gene, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Fitted expression", y = "Standardized residual")

qq_plot <- ggplot(residual_data, aes(sample = standardized_residual)) +
  stat_qq(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.7) +
  stat_qq_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ gene) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Theoretical normal quantile", y = "Observed residual quantile")

diagnostics <- cowplot::plot_grid(residual_plot, qq_plot, ncol = 1)
ggsave("results/figures/model_diagnostics.png", diagnostics,
       width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
ggsave("results/figures/model_diagnostics.pdf", diagnostics,
       width = 11, height = 7, bg = "white")
diagnostics
```

**What we see.** The residuals are centred on zero, and the clusters reflect
cell type (TLR4) or cell type and sex (KDM5D). In the Q–Q plots, all three
probes follow the line through the middle but have **heavier tails** than a
normal distribution, meaning a few arrays sit further from their fitted value
than expected. This is common in expression data.

Variance fractions are **descriptive** summaries, not hypothesis tests, so
modest departures from normality do not invalidate them. These plots are there
to catch gross problems, such as a handful of extreme arrays driving a result.

# Check 4: sensitivity analyses

Every analysis involves judgement calls. A sensitivity analysis repeats the
analysis with a different, equally defensible choice and asks whether the
conclusions change. We test two choices:

| Analysis | What changes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **All paired donors, no age** | Adds back the 9 donors with conflicting ages and drops `Age` from the model | Checks that excluding those donors did not shape the results |
| **Sex and cell type as fixed effects** | Codes sex and cell type as 0/1 fixed effects instead of random effects | Checks that the random-effect choice for two-level variables does not matter |

To save time, we run both on the same **2,000 randomly chosen probes**. A
random sample avoids favouring, say, only highly variable genes. We then
compare the results with the main model on those same probes.

```{r sensitivity-setup}
set.seed(20261104)
subset_ids <- sample(rownames(expression), 2000)
fwrite(data.frame(probe_id = subset_ids), "results/tables/sensitivity_probes.csv")

backend <- if (params$workers > 1) MulticoreParam(workers = params$workers) else SerialParam()

fit_sensitivity <- function(expression, metadata, formula) {
  result <- as.data.frame(fitExtractVarPartModel(expression, formula, metadata,
    REML = FALSE, useInitialFit = FALSE, BPPARAM = backend))
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(result), rownames(expression)),
            all(is.finite(as.matrix(result))),
            max(abs(rowSums(result) - 1)) < 1e-6)
  result
}

# Reuse a saved sensitivity fit when it exists (set `refit: true` to redo it).
fit_or_load_sensitivity <- function(name, expression, metadata, formula) {
  saved_file <- paste0("results/models/sensitivity_", name, ".rds")
  if (params$refit || !file.exists(saved_file)) {
    saveRDS(fit_sensitivity(expression, metadata, formula), saved_file)
  }
  result <- readRDS(saved_file)
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(result), rownames(expression)))  # same probes?
  result
}
```

```{r sensitivity-fits}
# (a) All 388 paired donors, without age.
paired <- droplevels(data$metadata[data$metadata$paired, ])
no_age_formula <- ~ (1 | Sex) + (1 | CellType) + (1 | Batch) + (1 | Individual)
all_paired <- fit_or_load_sensitivity(
  "All_paired_no_age",
  data$expression[subset_ids, paired$sample_id], paired, no_age_formula
)

# (b) Sex and cell type as numeric 0/1 fixed effects.
fixed_metadata <- metadata
fixed_metadata$Sex      <- as.numeric(fixed_metadata$Sex == "Male")
fixed_metadata$CellType <- as.numeric(fixed_metadata$CellType == "Monocyte")
fixed_formula <- ~ Age + Sex + CellType + (1 | Batch) + (1 | Individual)
binary_fixed <- fit_or_load_sensitivity(
  "Binary_fixed",
  expression[subset_ids, ], fixed_metadata, fixed_formula
)

c(paired_donors = nlevels(paired$Individual), paired_arrays = nrow(paired))
```

## Compare with the main model

We compare in two ways:

* **Median fractions:** does the typical probe look the same?
* **Spearman correlation**, per component, between each sensitivity fit and the
  main model. A value near 1 means probes keep the **same ranking**. The probes
  with high donor variance in the main model also have high donor variance in
  the alternative model.

```{r sensitivity-compare}
sensitivities <- list(
  Primary_subset    = models$Combined[subset_ids, ],
  All_paired_no_age = all_paired,
  Binary_fixed      = binary_fixed
)

summaries    <- list()
correlations <- list()
for (name in names(sensitivities)) {
  result <- sensitivities[[name]]
  fwrite(data.frame(probe_id = rownames(result), result),
         paste0("results/tables/", name, ".csv"))

  summaries[[name]] <- data.frame(
    model          = name,
    component      = names(result),
    median_percent = 100 * vapply(result, median, numeric(1)),
    row.names      = NULL
  )

  if (name == "Primary_subset") next  # the reference; nothing to compare with
  components <- intersect(names(result), names(sensitivities$Primary_subset))
  correlations[[name]] <- data.frame(
    model     = name,
    component = components,
    spearman  = vapply(components, function(component) {
      cor(result[[component]], sensitivities$Primary_subset[[component]],
          method = "spearman")
    }, numeric(1))
  )
}
summaries    <- rbindlist(summaries)
correlations <- rbindlist(correlations)
fwrite(summaries,    "results/tables/sensitivity_summary.csv")
fwrite(correlations, "results/tables/sensitivity_correlations.csv")
```

Median % of variance explained (columns = analysis):

```{r sensitivity-medians}
knitr::kable(dcast(summaries, component ~ model, value.var = "median_percent"),
             digits = 2)
```

Spearman correlation with the main model (columns = analysis):

```{r sensitivity-correlations}
knitr::kable(dcast(correlations, component ~ model, value.var = "spearman"),
             digits = 3)
```

```{r sensitivity-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
sensitivity_plot <- ggplot(summaries, aes(component, median_percent, fill = model)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Median variance explained (%)", fill = NULL)

ggsave("results/figures/sensitivity_checks.png", sensitivity_plot,
       width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
ggsave("results/figures/sensitivity_checks.pdf", sensitivity_plot,
       width = 10, height = 5, bg = "white")
sensitivity_plot
```

```{r lowest-correlation, include = FALSE}
# Lowest correlation for a component across both analyses, rounded down.
lowest <- function(name) {
  sprintf("%.3f", floor(1000 * min(correlations[component == name]$spearman)) / 1000)
}
```

**How to read this.** The large components, cell type, donor and residual,
have similar medians in all three analyses. Their probe-by-probe correlations
with the main model are very high: at least `r lowest("CellType")` for cell
type and `r lowest("Individual")` for donor. The main conclusions therefore do not depend on these two modelling
choices. Correlations for tiny components such as batch and sex are less
informative, because most of their values are at or near zero.

# Record versions and a summary of the checks

Finally, we record exactly which package versions produced these results, and
write a short plain-text summary of the checks.

```{r record}
packages <- c("variancePartition", "lme4", "limma", "BiocParallel",
              "data.table", "ggplot2", "cowplot")
package_versions <- data.frame(
  package = packages,
  version = vapply(packages, function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)), character(1))
)
fwrite(package_versions, "results/package_versions.csv")
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = "results/sessionInfo.txt")

writeLines(c(
  "All three main models retained every probe; fractions are finite, nonnegative and sum to one.",
  sprintf("Independent optimizer comparison: %d probes per model; maximum difference %.6f percentage points.",
          length(audit_ids), 100 * max(audit$absolute_difference)),
  "Sensitivity analyses: 2,000 fixed random probes; expanded paired cohort without age; numeric fixed sex/cell effects.",
  "Residual diagnostics are saved separately; these variance fractions are descriptive point estimates."
), "results/checks.txt")

package_versions
```

# Summary

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Completeness | All `r format(nrow(expression), big.mark = ",")` probes fitted in all three models; every fraction is valid |
| Independent refit | `bobyqa` agrees to within `r signif(100 * max(audit$absolute_difference), 2)` percentage points |
| Residual diagnostics | Saved to `results/figures/model_diagnostics.png` for visual review |
| Sensitivity | Medians and probe rankings are stable for the main components |

This completes the analysis. The one-page summary is in
`report/ImmVar_summary.pdf`.
